q: Every SRPF subscriber is required to:

options.A: Make a nomination in the prescribed form
options.B: Take a loan in the first year

q: A subscriber may change the nomination:

options.B: Only after 10 years

q: If the subscriber has a family, the nomination must be in favour of:

options.B: Any person of choice
options.C: One or more members of the family

q: For SRPF purposes, family includes:

options.B: Only the spouse
options.C: Spouse, children and dependent parents or siblings

q: On the subscriber's death with a valid nomination, the balance is paid to:

options.B: The government
options.D: The nominee named in the nomination

q: If a subscriber dies without a valid nomination, the amount is:

options.A: Paid only to the eldest member
options.B: Kept in suspense permanently
options.D: Paid to family members in equal shares

q: If the nominee is a minor at the time of payment:

options.A: It is paid to the neighbours
options.B: The nomination is cancelled
options.D: It is paid to the guardian on the minor's behalf

q: A nomination in favour of a non-family person becomes invalid when the subscriber:

options.B: Acquires a family

q: If two persons are nominated without specifying shares, the amount is:

options.A: Paid fully to the first nominee
options.B: Shared equally between them

q: A later nomination made by the subscriber:

options.B: Supersedes the earlier nomination

q: If the nominee dies before the subscriber:

options.B: A fresh nomination should be made
options.C: The amount goes to the government

q: On retirement, the subscriber receives:

options.B: The balance at credit with interest up to payment

q: On transfer to another railway, the PF balance is:

options.A: Paid in cash to the subscriber
options.B: Transferred to the new accounts office

q: Interest on SRPF balances is:

options.B: Credited annually at the government-declared rate

q: A subscriber missing and unheard of for seven years is:

options.B: Presumed dead and payment made to the nominee or family

q: The nomination is submitted to:

options.B: The Head of Office or Accounts Officer

q: A nomination in favour of the spouse after the marriage is dissolved:

options.B: Ceases to be valid

q: For nomination purposes, an adopted child is:

options.B: Treated as a member of the family

q: On resignation from service, the subscriber is entitled to:

options.B: The balance at credit with interest

q: If a subscriber is dismissed from service:

options.B: The PF balance with interest remains payable

q: A non-refundable advance shortly before retirement is allowed:

options.B: Within 12 months before retirement for specified purposes

q: The nominee's right to the PF amount arises:

options.B: Only after the subscriber's death

q: If a subscriber dies in service, the family may additionally receive:

options.B: DCRG and family pension as admissible, besides PF

q: A subscriber having no family may nominate:

options.B: Any person

q: A valid nomination must be:

options.B: In writing in the prescribed form and duly accepted

q: Payment of the PF balance to the nominee is made:

options.B: With interest credited up to the date of payment
options.D: After one year of the claim

q: On permanent absorption in a public sector undertaking, the PF balance is:

options.B: Transferred or paid out as per rules

q: A fresh nomination becomes necessary when:

options.B: The earlier nominee dies or the nomination becomes invalid

q: The subscriber's own subscriptions with interest form:

options.B: The subscriber's personal accumulation in the fund

q: A guardian receiving PF on behalf of a minor nominee must:

options.B: Hold and use it for the minor's benefit
